clue.text: Wonderful bananas of usual breadth

indicators.note: to go bananas is to go crazy, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for breadth

explanation.surface: Someone admires bananas of a perfectly ordinary width.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit but is slang for mad, the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal praise meaning marvellous, extraordinary or terrific.

clue.text: In Versailles I initially abhorred miserable envy

parts.note: je is French for I, and Versailles places us in France

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of abhorred
lousy is informal for wretched or miserable

explanation.surface: A visitor to the French palace confesses to hating their wretched envy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Versailles' tells you to put the I into French, giving JE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy and envy are close synonyms for resentment of what another person has.

clue.text: Benign deity full of love

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a deity is a god
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A kindly god overflowing with love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as O comes from tennis scoring, where love means nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign describes something kindly or harmless, a plain synonym of decent and wholesome.

clue.text: An ideal place for everyone, the best current answer

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages
the top is the best
I is the symbol for electric current
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a perfect place open to all as the finest solution going.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal viewing; I is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More named his imagined perfect society Utopia, and the word now means any imagined perfect society.

clue.text: Urban guy wants money up front? No, that's dodgy

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or unsound, so the letters are not to be trusted in their given order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: up front means at the very start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of money
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city slicker asks for cash in advance, and the speaker refuses because it looks shady.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'No' read as dialogue, but NO is just more letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A townsman is a man who lives in a town or city, so an urban male.

clue.text: Locate bad smell for questionable treatment

parts.note: to locate something is to place it
BO stands for body odour

explanation.surface: Tracking down a nasty odour leads to some dubious medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: BO, short for body odour, is a stock crossword abbreviation for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert pill or procedure with no active effect, so its value as medicine is doubtful.

clue.text: Spot on fruit we gather

indicators.note: to gather is to learn by hearsay, so what follows is what we are told rather than what is written

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit; the target word is said identically with a silent B

explanation.surface: Pickers note a blemish on the fruit they harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a mark on fruit, but 'Spot on' is one phrase meaning exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb as an adverb means exactly or precisely, as in plumb in the middle, the sense of a plumb line.

clue.text: Snake around much of The Prancing Pony

indicators.note: much of a thing is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes
around means surrounding, so one set of letters is wrapped about the other
prancing is high-stepping and capering, so these letters leap about out of order

parts.note: taken as written
the word with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A serpent coils round the inn in Tolkien's Bree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prancing Pony is the inn in The Lord of the Rings, so the phrase reads as a name; split it and 'Prancing' becomes the scramble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A python is a large constricting snake of Africa, Asia and Australia.

clue.text: Peer is with four in lavatory

indicators.note: with here means having something about it, carried inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to peer nosily is to pry
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A nobleman shares a toilet with four others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' suggests a lord, but here it is the verb to look closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A privy is an old word for a toilet, especially an outdoor one.

clue.text: Umlaut's dotty on both sides

indicators.note: dotty means crazy or scatterbrained, so the letters fall into a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An umlaut is literally dots over a letter, and the clue jokes that it has dots on either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' fits an umlaut's two dots so well that it reads as description, not as the signal for madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mutual is shared or reciprocated, felt or done by each party toward the other.

clue.text: Fat duke's tearing off

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
ripping is tearing off

explanation.surface: A portly aristocrat is tearing away at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' reads as an adjective for the duke, but it is a noun; dripping is a British cooking fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dripping is the fat that runs from roasting meat, kept for frying or spreading on bread.

clue.text: Quite skilfully packaging instrument on special order

indicators.note: to package something is to wrap it up, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: ably means skilfully

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means placed after, so the word preceding this signal is written later

parts.note: SO as initials for special order
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is packed up expertly for a custom order.
explanation.walkthrough: Quite here is the emphatic reply, as in 'Quite!', meaning completely so.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words serve as an emphatic agreement or as an intensifier meaning totally or entirely.

clue.text: Sex god accepts universal currency

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece is received inside the other

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of desire
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: A god of love takes payment in the money everyone uses.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural answer fits 'currency' because euros are units of a currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Euros are the money units used across most European Union member states.

clue.text: A lot of men in farmyard

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following word

parts.note: the letters run inside this word

explanation.surface: A crowd of men gather in a farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits whole inside a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large organised body of soldiers, so in loose terms a multitude of men.

clue.text: Mixed-up loveless saddo — they have issues with women

indicators.note: loveless means without love, which in crosswords is the round zero, so that character goes
mixed-up means confused and jumbled, so the order is scrambled

parts.note: the word without its O, love as zero

explanation.surface: A messed-up loser is described as having problems with women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' sounds like emotional baggage, but issue also means offspring; fathers have children with women. A saddo is British slang for a sad, pathetic person.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is an old legal word for children, and fathers produce children with their partners.

clue.text: Adjustable chair — and it might be found on the web

definitions.text: it might be found on the web

indicators.note: something adjustable can be altered and reset, so the letters are moved into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An office chair advertised as something you can buy online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The web' suggests the internet, but it is a spider's web.
explanation.definitionFit: Arachnids are the class including spiders, which sit on webs they spin.

clue.text: Stories for instance, going back, enthralling a lot of sailors

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece is held within the other
going back means travelling backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: say, as in 'say, a cat', means for instance
RN is the Royal Navy, a great many sailors

explanation.surface: Tales, perhaps from long ago, that captivate a crew of seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors spinning stories is the scene, and yarns are exactly what sailors spin.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long, often exaggerated tale, the classic sailor's story.

clue.text: Table tennis after two sopranos push out pianos for choral revel

indicators.note: to push out is to oust and take the place of, so one letter displaces another

parts.note: ping-pong is another name for table tennis
S is the abbreviation for soprano, twice
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly, twice

explanation.surface: Two singers displace the pianists after a ping-pong game to get a party singing.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ps of the game's other name give way to an S each.
explanation.definitionFit: A sing-song is an informal gathering where people sing together for fun.

clue.text: Split money for accommodation

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the regular payment for a home

explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads like sharing the money, but it is a separate meaning: torn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of rend, to tear, and also the periodic payment a tenant owes a landlord.

clue.text: Star on the left with density rising far off

parts.note: red describes the political left

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top
off means gone bad or awry, so the letters are out of their usual order

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
D is the abbreviation for density
taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomer spots a distant star to the left that is growing denser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far off' reads as distant, but only 'far' is letters and 'off' scrambles them. Red Dwarf is also a British sci-fi sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: A red dwarf is a small, cool, faint type of star, the commonest kind in the galaxy.

clue.text: Young Ones dressed up as nothing short of old

indicators.note: dressed up means disguised in costume, so the letters appear in an altered form
short of means lacking, so something is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Young Ones, a 1980s British student sitcom, has its cast in costume looking like nothing but old men.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD loses its O to leave LD, which is mixed with AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lads are boys or young men, so youngsters in the plural sense.

clue.text: Increased intervals between square and measured steps

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for square
to pace is to walk with measured steps

explanation.surface: Someone widened the gaps between a square and a series of carefully counted footsteps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measured steps' is a verb phrase in disguise: paced means walked with even strides.
explanation.definitionFit: To space things out is to set gaps between them, so the past tense means made the gaps larger.

clue.text: A problem with the wet amid spring dances

indicators.note: dancing letters skip and whirl about, ending in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wet weather spoils spring festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wet' sounds like rainy weather, but it means moisture. Rising Damp is also a British sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising damp is groundwater seeping up through masonry walls, a common fault in old houses.

clue.text: Liquid nitrogen stored in broken urn — ultimately leaky

indicators.note: something stored in a vessel is kept inside it
broken means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of leaky

explanation.surface: Liquid nitrogen kept in a cracked urn ends up seeping out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid nitrogen' reads as one substance, but 'Liquid' is the definition and 'nitrogen' only N.
explanation.definitionFit: Runny describes something flowing freely, like a thin fluid, so it means fluid or watery.

clue.text: Half-hearted Gollum could become this influential individual

indicators.note: half-hearted suggests the heart is partly missing, so one of the doubled central letters is dropped
could become means might turn into, so the letters change their arrangement

parts.note: Tolkien's creature with one of its middle Ls removed

explanation.surface: A timid Gollum might be transformed into a powerful figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Gollum's heart is the double L at its centre; losing half of it leaves one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a magnate, a powerful person in business or media, from the Mughal emperors.

clue.text: Product of explosive shell part, no ends missing

indicators.note: with ends missing, each word loses its final letter
an explosion blasts things apart, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the word without its last letter
the word without its last letter
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: What a bursting shell throws out, intact pieces and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' does double duty, belonging to the definition and also scrambling the trimmed words.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is the metal fragments thrown out when a bomb or artillery round bursts.

clue.text: Prison island held by the French for endless sentence

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

parts.note: le is French for the
the Château d'If is a prison on an island off Marseille, made famous by The Count of Monte Cristo

explanation.surface: A French island jail holds someone serving a term that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is not I but IF, home of the fortress prison in Dumas's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A life term is imprisonment for the rest of one's days, with no fixed release date.

clue.text: Half of rise added to income? — refuse to get carried away

parts.note: the second half of the word
a wage is income from work

explanation.surface: An employee wonders whether only half of a pay rise was added, and refuses to get excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, as in decline, but it is the noun meaning waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is waste water and excrement carried off through drains and sewers.

clue.text: Promising a flower to border most of famous garden

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter
to border something is to run along its edges, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a lily is a flower
Kew Gardens in London, the famous botanic garden, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A gardener hopes to edge a well-known garden with flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is Britain's best-known botanic garden, in southwest London.
explanation.definitionFit: A likely candidate is one who shows promise and seems apt to succeed.

clue.text: Sombre event's gone wild outside one local

parts.note: feral describes a tame animal gone wild

explanation.surface: A solemn occasion turned rowdy outside a neighbourhood pub, the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone wild' is a definition of FERAL, not a scramble signal, and 'local' marks the regional 'un rather than a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral is a ceremony for the dead, a solemn and mournful gathering.
